objective: The Hooks Store, job 13: the Promotions panel redone, ad-blocker-safe markup, RPC fallbacks and the proven-line edge case. Read SPEC.md at its current version (1.54, decisions 43 to 47) in https://github.com/the-hook-store/hooks-store-spec and the section "Carry-overs for job 13" of jobs/next-job-carry-overs.md there (raw: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/the-hook-store/hooks-store-spec/main/jobs/next-job-carry-overs.md) for the full wording and tests of every item; every item is in scope. (n) Promotions panel, balance first then hooks (SPEC 3.5, decision 44): replace the four-step "Promote a hook" flow with the terms sentence; the promotion chain selector (where the wallet pays); "In your wallet on <chain>: N IMD" and "Deposited for promotions: N IMD"; a DEPOSIT box with a typed IMD amount (an approval only when the allowance is short, then one deposit) and WITHDRAW for the unspent deposit; then one row per live hook the wallet launched on either chain, labelled with its chain, with PROMOTE (the free listing created first and silently when the hook has none on that chain, then purchase for 24 hours paid from the deposit; disabled with "Deposit at least 0.1 IMD first" below 0.1 IMD) and, for a running placement, hours left, total paid, rank, BOOST (typed amount from the deposit, the non-refundable sentence, a confirmation) and CANCEL (pro-rata refund to the deposit, boosts forfeited, explained first); a third line "Earned as recipient: N IMD" with WITHDRAW PROCEEDS when the wallet is the recipient; every transaction simulated first; all balances re-read after each. Tests: unit tests for the allowance decision and the disabled states; Playwright with a controlled RPC and local wallet: deposit 0.25, promote one hook, boost 0.05, cancel, withdraw; a wallet with 0 deposit sees PROMOTE disabled with the note. (o) Public RPC fallback (SPEC 7.2, decision 45): site-config.json lists RPC URLs per chain (Ethereum: https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com, https://rpc.mevblocker.io, https://eth.llamarpc.com; Robinhood Chain: https://rpc.mainnet.chain.robinhood.com plus a second public endpoint the builder verifies), the chain clients use viem's fallback transport with one retry, and "Could not read promotions on <chain>" or any other RPC error line appears only after every endpoint failed; a unit test on the config shape and a Playwright case where the first endpoint answers 429 and the strip still renders. (p) Ad-blocker-safe markup (SPEC 3.1, decision 46): the strip's cards use className adcard, which EasyList's generic rule ##.adcard hides on every site, so visitors with uBlock Origin, AdBlock Plus, AdGuard or Brave see an empty band. Rename every element of the strip and the Promotions panel so no class, id or attribute value matches a generic cosmetic filter (placement-card, placement-slot, featured-band, featured-track, featured-group, promotion-row; never ad, ads, adcard, adslot, ad-card, sponsored or promo as a class or id; the #AD text label stays); a unit test loads the generic cosmetic rules from a pinned copy of EasyList in the repository, refreshed at build time from https://easylist.to/easylist/easylist.txt, and asserts no class or id in dist/ matches any ##.class or ###id rule; a Playwright case injects those rules as a stylesheet and asserts the placement card and the open-slot card stay visible. (q) Proven line for an exact stack on the other chain (SPEC 4.17, decision 47): when a draft's blocks exactly match a proven launch deployed on the other chain, the line reads "Adapted from a proven launch: <name> (launch <n>, audited <date>): the same blocks, redeployed on <chain>" and the request's start-from sentence says "keep its behavior, deploy on <chain> with that chain's PoolManager <address>, apply the parameters and rules of this request", never "removes none and adds none"; unit tests for both chains and for a nearest match on the other chain. Deliver source, dist/ and test results.
